Select the fisheye projection model to use.

Stereographic (little planet) (focal * tan(ray_angle): Notably some Samyang fisheye lenses fall in this category

Equidistant (equiangular) (focal * ray_angle): This is considered the 'ideal' reference model for fisheye distortion. The equidistant projection can be used to create an Angular Map.

Equisolid (equal area) (2 * focal * sin(ray_angle/2)): The majority of fisheye lenses fall in this category.

Orthographic (sine law) (focal * sin(ray_angle)): Uncommon lens model found in specialty lenses such as the Yasuhara Madoka 180The equisolid projection can be used to create the image of a texture-mapped ball from infinitely far away.

Specify the output format

Format	Specify which format to use or how to compute it starting from the input.

To Format	Force the specified format as output format. When using camera type projections (e.g. rectilinear), the sensor size height parameter will be ignored.

To Width	Output format will have specified width, while height will be computed according to the output projection type ratio.

To Scale	Output format will have its width computed from the input format width, while height will be computed according to the output projection type ratio.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

description.plain_text: SphericalTransform: Transform between different projections for inputs and outputs. In addition to projection, the plugin can add an input and an output rotation, which are symmetrical to each other. A translation is also possible by specifying camera position for rectilinear and fisheye projections. This is enacted by projecting the translated cameras onto a sphere at a distance specified by the convergence parameter. The plugin supports the following hotkeys: Ctrl+Alt+Left Mouse Drag: Rotate the output Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Left Mouse Drag: Rotate the output along vertical or horizontal axis only Ctrl+Alt+Right Mouse Drag: Change the output focal length for camera projections
description.text:
SphericalTransform: Transform between different projections for inputs and outputs.

In addition to projection, the plugin can add an input and an output rotation, which are symmetrical to each other. A translation is also possible by specifying camera position for rectilinear and fisheye projections. This is enacted by projecting the translated cameras onto a sphere at a distance specified by the convergence parameter.
The plugin supports the following hotkeys:

Ctrl+Alt+Left Mouse Drag: Rotate the output

Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Left Mouse Drag: Rotate the output along vertical or horizontal axis only

Ctrl+Alt+Right Mouse Drag: Change the output focal length for camera projections
